guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster (first one in the UK)
models: Fender Stratocaster (first one in the UK)
guitar.notes: Hank Marvin famously owned the first Fender Stratocaster imported to the UK (a salmon-pink/Fiesta Red one), a well-documented and historically significant guitar/guitarist pairing.

tone.target: bright surf clean with spring reverb and tremolo
tone.profile: bright surf clean with spring reverb and tremolo
tone.summary: A pristine, twangy signal chain featuring a clean boost, mild compression, US Deluxe amp simulation, paired with a 2x12 cab, finished with prominent Tremolo, Spring Reverb, and Digital Delay for that signature bright surf effect.
corrections: favor spring reverb over generic reverb

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean tones.

blocks.purpose: Smooth out dynamics and add sustain for single-note clarity.
blocks.gap: None. Compression is key for controlled twang.

blocks.purpose: Provide a subtle grit and warmth without adding crunch or fuzz.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used for gentle breakup, simulating the slight dirt of an old Fender tube amp. A dedicated clean boost might be better, but this provides necessary character.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, clean, and articulate tone of a Fender-style amplifier.
blocks.gap: None. This is the core sound source for surf rock.

blocks.purpose: Provide the characteristic bright and open sound of a smaller American cabinet.
Brighten the high end and enhance single-note clarity.
blocks.gap: None. Used for surgical tone shaping.

blocks.purpose: Bypass. The target tone explicitly avoids wah effects.
Add the signature rhythmic vibrato essential for surf rock.
Provide the classic, bright spring reverb associated with surf music.
blocks.gap: None. Crucial effect specified in the verdict.

blocks.purpose: Add rhythmic space and echo to the single-note leads.
blocks.gap: While not mandatory, a subtle delay enhances the 'twang' and spaciousness required for surf music.

improvements.summary: The current IR is good, but a dedicated vintage Fender-style cabinet will enhance the authentic bright twang and open sound required for classic surf rock.

proposals.reason: Enhance authentic bright, open twang of vintage surf sound.
